exposure: Gestational age (28-31 weeks, 32-36 weeks, >37 weeks, <28 weeks)
outcome: Birth trauma (intracranial laceration and haemorrhage, injuries to scalp, injuries to central and peripheral nervous system, fractures to skeleton, facial and eye injury)
cohort: 62,330 singleton pregnancies delivered after 24 weeks gestation
finding: While birth trauma was more common in spontaneous vaginal deliveries, when stratified by severity, preterm babies delivered vaginally did not have a higher risk of major birth trauma compared to those delivered by CS.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was not protective against birth injuries.
